en: The Moon's gravity is one-sixth of Earth's, meaning a person who weighs 600 newtons on Earth would weigh only 100 newtons there.
A crowbar with an effort arm 100 centimeters long and a load arm 10 centimeters long multiplies your pushing force by exactly ten times.
The friction between rubber tires and dry asphalt is about 0.7, but it drops to just 0.1 when the road is covered in wet ice.
Earth's magnetic north pole is currently about 500 kilometers away from the geographic North Pole and moves roughly 50 kilometers every year.
A single lightning bolt transfers about 300 megajoules of electrical energy to the ground, enough to power a 100-watt bulb for 35 days.
Light travels at 300,000 kilometers per second in a vacuum, but slows down to 225,000 kilometers per second when passing through water.
Sound travels through air at 343 meters per second, but it moves almost 15 times faster through solid steel at 5,120 meters per second.
Copper conducts heat over 1,000 times faster than wood, which is why a metal pot handle gets hot much quicker than a wooden spoon.
A 1,000-kilogram car moving at 20 meters per second has four times more kinetic energy than the same car moving at just 10 meters per second.
A block and tackle pulley system with four supporting ropes reduces the effort needed to lift a 400-newton box to just 100 newtons.
If you double the distance between two objects, the gravitational pull between them becomes exactly four times weaker, not just two times weaker.
Wrapping 50 coils of wire around an iron nail creates a stronger electromagnet than wrapping only 10 coils around the exact same nail.
